name: Hobab
overview: Hobab is a male figure identified in Scripture as the son of Reuel, who is also known as Moses' father-in-law. Beyond this familial connection, little else is detailed about his tribe or additional background. His mention is concise, focusing primarily on his relationship within Moses' extended family.
namesAndTitles: The name Hobab means 'beloved' and possibly 'deceit' in Hebrew. This proper name is not indicated as being given by God, but it reflects a personal designation noted in Numbers 10:29.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Hobab as the son of Reuel and infers that he is Moses' brother-in-law through this connection. No other family relationships are documented beyond these ties.
scriptureSignificance: Hobab's significance centers on his familial link to Moses, serving as a close relative through marriage. His mention in Numbers 10:29 situates him within the narrative of Israel's wilderness journey, highlighting the role of Moses' extended family in the community's leadership and support. While details about his personal actions are sparse, his presence underscores the interconnectedness of Moses’ household during a pivotal period in Israel's history.
